keywords: 怎么用 HistoryPanel 做数据分析
title: HistoryPanel research transforms, not a full backtest
summary: On an existing panel, compute research series—returns, volatility, kline indicators, where masks, ranks, and coarse portfolio checks. This is research, not Operator/Backtester.
narrative:
Once you have a HistoryPanel, this card covers research transforms on that panel.

Time helpers include shift, diff, and pct_change. Price-aware helpers include returns and volatility (including adj columns such as close|b when the root resolves). Indicators come from hp.kline.*, research_preset, apply_ta, and candle_pattern. Cross-section tools include rank and zscore (cs/ts). where builds research masks. cum_return, normalize, and portfolio(..., benchmark=...) are coarse study helpers—they omit fees, settlement, and MOQ.

assign and expr here mean derive research columns from existing ones. align_to and resample are hygiene before IC or portfolio work, not a lesson on creating the first panel.

research_preset can add indicator columns in one call. Charting those columns is a separate plot topic: hp.plot() does not invent MACD or SMA columns for you.

HistoryPanel research is not a full backtest. Fees, settlement, MOQ, and trade reports belong to Operator and Backtester. When you are ready for a formal run, switch to Plan and ask about built-in backtest; Ask will not emit a plan_id from this card.

This card does not teach 3-D shape or slice basics, and it does not walk the advanced 2.6–2.8 closed loops.
python_code:
import qteasy as qt
hp = qt.get_kline(htypes='close', shares='000001.SZ, 000002.SZ', start='20230101', end='20230630', as_panel=True)
r = hp.returns()
print(r.htypes)
risk_notes: portfolio and cum_return are research aggregates. Do not treat them as audited backtest performance. Ask never invents return numbers.
